families, &c. Note the thrice-repeated fourfold division in vv. 5, 20. See Ap. 10.
divided: i.e. in judgment. Cp. v. 25. Here parad = disruption in judgment. God's division (v. 25) included ZION. Man's disruption included BABYLON (11. 2, 9).

earth = people of the earth. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject). Ap. 6; "earth" put for inhabitants. language. Heb. "lip". Fig. Metonymy (of cause), Ap. 6; lip put for language. The chapter begins with man's attempt to unify mankind, and ends with God's new provision to unify all in blessing with Abraham's seed.
from the east = eastward. Shinar = Babylonia.

said. Sin with their tongues punished in the same manner (v. 7). burn, &c. Heb. brick bricks, and burn a burning. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6, emphasising their determination. Burning in fire, not waiting for sun. See note on "brick-kiln", 2 Sam. 12. 31. slime = bitumen. So tenacious to-day that detachment almost impossible. Cp. the slime of Babel with the jewels of Zion (Rev. 21. 19).

may reach. No Ellipsis here. Heb. "and its top with the heavens", i.e. with the Zodiac depicted on it, as in ancient temples of Denderah and Esneh in Egypt. a name. Manifesting independence of God. Nimrod being the rebel leader. See 10. 8-10, and cp. 12. 2.
came down. Fig. Anthropopatheia (Ap. 6).
Go to, let Us go down. This is always in judgment (cp. 18. 21. Ex. 3. 8). Here in contrast with v. 4, to man's "Go to, let us go up". Fig. Anthropopatheia, Ap. 6. See v. 5.
scattered. Sept. same word as in Acts 8. 1 (Isa. 8. 9). This was to preserve the revelation contained in the Zodiac and the constellations.

Babel. Heb. = confusion. Cp. Job 5. 12, another application of the Hebrew word. scatter. Sept. same word as in Acts 8. 1. Result of which was the conversion of the Ethiopian (Acts 8. 26), of HAM. Saul (Acts 9), of SHEM. Cornelius (Acts 10), of JAPHETH. Tongues confounded in judgment (Gen. 11. 9). Given in grace (Acts 2. 4). United in glory (Rev. 7. 9).
11. 10-26 (I, p. 1). THE GENERATIONS OF SHEM.
Shem. A return to the main purpose of the Book. See note on 5. 32.
Salah. Luke 3. 36 says Cainan, but this was probably a gloss from Sept., and crept into the text. No second Cainan in Heb. text here or elsewhere. Cp. 1 Chron. 1. 18.
Eber. See above, 10. 24. Peleg born (10. 25) 14 years before v. 9.
Peleg. See above, 10. 25 (Luke 3. 35, Phalec).
Serug born (Luke 3. 35, Saruch).
Terah. Name prob. = traveller.
Generations of Terah. The centre of the eleven. See page 1 and Ap. 29. Abram the youngest comes first (born 1996). Cp. Shem (10. 21), Jacob (25. 23; 27. 15), Ephraim (48. 20).
before his father. The first death so recorded. Ur = the Uru or "city" of the cuneiform texts. Now = Mugheir on W. bank of Euphrates.
Iscah. See Ap. 29.

Terah took. Terah being 200 and Abram 70. Cp. 15. 7. Josh. 24. 3. Neh. 9. 7. Acts 7. 2-4. Heb. 11. 8. daughter in law = daughter by another wife. See Ap. 29. they. Others beside those named. Cp. 24. 10, 15; 29. 10. Ur = a city of great pretensions. Recent excavations show luxury and attainments. Abraham no nomad. See note on 11. 28. Haran. Not the Haran of v. 26 above; but Charran (Acts 7. 2, 4), the frontier town of Bab. Empire, devoted to the worship of the Moon-god. dwelt. Till he died (v. 32).
died in Haran (Charran). With this Acts 7. 4 agrees. Not seeing this, the Massorites wrongly marked v. 32 with an inverted Nun as being a dislocation of the Text.

LORD = Jehovah, "The God of Glory" of Acts 7. 2. Fig. Enallage = The Glorious God, in contrast with idols (Josh. 24. 2). Get thee out = Go for thyself, i.e. whatever others may do. Death had broken the link of nature's tie, which hindered Abram's obedience. kindred. Leaving Nahor and his family (except Lot), 24. 4, 10-15; 25. 20; 28. 7-10. shew. See Heb. 11. 8.
And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6). I will. Note this sevenfold promise with the sevenfold blessing in Ex. 6. 4-8 (Ap. 10).
thee. To Abraham personally. See note on 50. 24.

seventy and five. The Law was 430 years "after" this (Ex. 12. 40. Gal. 3. 17). Abram 100 when Isaac born, and 105 when Isaac recognised as his "seed" (Gen. 21. 12). This 25 + 5 explains the 400 years of Gen. 15. 13 and Acts 7. 6. See note on 15. 13.
souls. Heb. pl. of nephesh = souls. See Ap. 13. they came. This time: not when they had started from Chaldea (11. 31).

Sichem. The place of Abram's first altar and Christ's first mission (John 4). Also of Jacob's altar (33. 18). Canaanite ... then in the land. It is evident that from Terah's and Abraham's call, Satan knew the line by which "the seed of the woman" (3. 15) was coming into the world. In ch. 6 he aimed at the whole human race. Now he aims at Abraham and his land. Here is the second explanation of the words "after that" in 6. 4. He pre-occupies the territory ready to dispute the advance. The Canaanite "was then" = "being already" there (cp. 13. 7). The progeny of the later attempt to corrupt the race had to be destroyed by the sword of Israel, as those "in the days of Noah" had been by the Flood. See Ap. 23 and 25. was = being. then = already.
altar. See note on Sichem, v. 6.

Beth-el. An ancient Canaanite sacred pillar, doubtless here from previous times, called Luz (28. 19; 35. 6; 48. 3. Josh. 16. 2; 18. 13. Judg. 1. 23). Cp. Judg. 1. 26. When Moses wrote he used the later name. altar. Between Beth-el and Ai would probably be Gerizim and Ebal, which were already or thus became sacred places. Cp. Deut. 27. 2, 12 and Josh. 8. 9, 30.
south. Heb. the Negeb or hill country S. of Judah (cp. 13. 1, 3). The Egyptian texts mention the Negeb. Towns taken by Shishak are mentioned as being there, e.g. Jerahmeel, Gerar, Kadesh, and Gaza.

famine. Satan's attempt (thus early) to destroy Abraham's seed, through Sarah. See Ap. 23. Thirteen (Ap. 10) famines recorded, 12. 10; 26. 1; 41. 54. Ruth 1. 1. 2 Sam. 21. 1. 1 Kings 18. 2. 2 Kings 4. 38; 7. 4; 25. 3. Neh. 5. 3. Jer. 14. 1. Luke 15. 14. Acts 11. 28. down. Always "down" to Egypt! Cp. Isa. 30. 2; 31. 1.

see thee. In Egypt the women went unveiled. kill me. Satan's next assault, working on Abraham's fear. If God had not interfered (v. 17), where would His promise have been? (3. 15; 12. 7; 13. 15, &c.). See Ap. 23 and 25.
sister. See note on 20. 12 and Ap. 29. my soul = I, myself. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13. Fig. Synecdoche (of Part), Ap. 6.
Pharaoh = the official title of all kings of Egypt, like Kaiser, Czar, &c.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton. See Ap. 6, emph. each class of property. All these pictured on the Monuments in Egypt. sheep, &c. No horses in Egypt till 18th Dynasty.
LORD. Divine intervention necessary. Ap. 23, 25.
What? Why? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton. See Ap. 6.
up = Palestine an ascent from Egypt. south = Heb. the Negeb, S. of Judea, N. from Egypt. Cp. 11. 9.
silver, and in gold: scarce in Palestine, but plentiful in Egypt.
tent: shows him a stranger. at the beginning: very significant. No altar for Abram in Egypt. between Beth-el and Hai. Prob Ebal or Gerizim. See note on 12. 8.
altar: shows him to be a worshipper. at the first. No worship in Egypt. See note v. 3.
tents. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject): "tents" put for the dwellers therein.
them. Those two. For signification of the No. 2, see Ap. 10.

strife. The first step in Lot's downward course. Note Lot's six downward steps: v. 7, "strife"; v. 10, "beheld"; v. 11, "chose"; v. 12, "pitched toward"; ch. 14. 12, "dwelt in"; 19. 1, "sat in its gate", as a ruler and citizen. See Ap. 10. Canaanite and Perizzite. See on 12. 6. These were the Nephilim. See Ap. 23, 25. dwelled. Heb. were dwelling. then = already. See note on 12. 6. in the land. Occupying it in advance, and spreading later to "the giant cities of Bashan".
brethren. Put by Synecdoche (of Species), for relatives. Ap. 6.
Is not the whole land, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. thou wilt take. Fig. Complex Ellipsis. See Ap. 6.

well watered. Great contrast with Palestine after the famine; and likeness to the fertility of Egypt. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. Sodom = flaming, burning. Gomorrah = people of fear: already mixed up in the sins of the Nephilim. 2 Pet. 2. 4. Jude 6.
chose. Lot lifted up his own eyes (v. 10), and made his own choice. Cp. Abram, v. 14.
cities = one of the cities. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Whole). See Ap. 6. Or "among the cities". Cp. v. 18. toward Sodom. See note on v. 7.
A parenthetical statement to show the nature of Lot's choice. Fig. Parenthesis. Ap. 6. wicked and sinners = very wicked sinners. Fig. Hendiadys. See Ap. 6, and Ap. 44, viii and xiii.
Lift up. God chose for Abraham; strictly topographical. See note v. 11. look. Note Abraham's four "looks": 13. 14 (earth); 15. 5 (heaven); 18. 2 (Jehovah); 22. 13 (a substitute).

to thee. Repeated to Isaac (26. 3), and to Jacob (28. 13; 35. 12). See note on 50. 24. for ever. Hence Israel is "the everlasting nation", Isa. 44. 7. "To thee" ensures resurrection. Cp. Ex. 3. 6 and Matt. 22. 23-33.
dust. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. In ch. 15. 5, as the "stars", marking the two parties in Israel: the earthly and heavenly (Heb. 11. 9-16); partakers of "the heavenly calling" (Heb. 3. 1).
thee. See note on 50. 24.
plain = among the oaks belonging to Mamre, brother of Eshcol and Aner (14. 13). Hebron, a later name used here. See notes on 23. 2 and Num. 13. 22.

came to pass in the days of. Heb. v'yahi bemeyi: occurs 6 times (see Ap. 10); always marks a time of trouble ending in blessing. Cp. Ruth 1. 1. Isa. 7. 1. Jer. 1. 3. Est. 1. 1. 2 Sam. 21. 1 (cp. v. 14). in the days. Dated in the reign of a king of Babylon: the united forces led by a king of Elam. The Assyrian tablets show that Elam had conquered and overrun Babylonia. Amraphel reigned in N. (Shinar); Eri-Aku (Arioch), an Elamite prince, in the S. at Larsa (Ellasar). All the names here are found on one tablet. Amraphel = Khammurabi of the Tablets. Ammurapi is Amraphel transliterated. Arioch = Eri-aku of the Tablets, in which it is found that his mother was sister to Chedorlaomer. Chedorlaomer = the Kudur-Lahgumal of the Tablets. Tidal = the Tudghula of the Tablets. nations. The Tablet says "he assembled the Ummanmanda", or the barbarian tribes of the Kurdish mountains, and that he "did evil" to the land of Bel. The Assyrian tablets are therefore shown to be correct by their agreement with Genesis.
Zoar. Cp. v. 8 and 19. 22.
vale. Afterward, the Salt (or Dead Sea), when Moses wrote. Siddim = the Siddim.

Twelve. The No. of Government. See Ap. 10. served = had served. v. 4 goes back to the events leading up to the present war with Sodom. thirteenth. The first occ. Hence the No. of Rebellion. See Ap. 10.

Rephaim = a branch of the Nephilim. See Ap. 25. Superhuman beings, so called after one Rapha: as the Anakim after Anak. See 15. 20. Deut. 2. 11, 20, 21; 3. 11, 13. Josh. 12. 4; 13. 12; 15. 8; 17. 15; 18. 16. See notes on 6. 4; 12. 6; 13. 7; 14. 5; 15. 20, 21. Zuzims in Ham, same as Zam-zummim in Cuneiform writing. Cp. Deut. 2. 20. Emim. Cp. Deut. 2. 10.
Horites. Deut. 2. 12.
En-mishpat = the spring of judgment. Not yet Kadesh = the Sanctuary. all the country. Heb. "the whole field", put by Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, for country.
takes up the present war with Sodom. Zoar. Cp. v. 2 and 19. 22.
four kings with five. See the No. 9, the number of Judgment. See Ap. 10.
slimepits = pits of bitumen, still a feature of the shores of the Dead Sea.
who dwelt: emph. to call attention to ch. 13. 12. See note. Heb. HE (Lot), being a dweller in Sodom.

Hebrew. So called from 'Eber (11. 14. Cp. 10. 21; 39. 14; 41. 12. Num. 24. 24), from 'abar, "to pass on" = "he who passed over from beyond" (Gr. hyper), i.e. beyond the Euphrates (Josh. 24. 2). he: emph. in contrast with Lot. these: emph. = these also having a covenant with Abram. See 13. 17.

trained = initiated or instructed, prob. in the worship of Jehovah. Cp. 12. 5; 15. 2; 18. 19; 24. 12-29; and Prov. 22. 6 (same word). 318 = a multiple of 6, the No. of "man". See Ap. 10. Dan. Not the Dan of Judges 18. 29, but a city in N. of Palestine long before the Danites changed the name of Laish.
he and his servants. Note the emphasis on "he".
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton. See Ap. 6.
king's dale = the king of Salem mentioned in next verse. The name still retained in 2 Sam. 18. 18.

Note the parenthetical clause (18-20), which interrupts in order to interpret. Melchizedek = King of righteousness, or by Fig. Enallage (Ap. 6), righteous king. In History, Gen. 14. In Prophecy, Ps. 110. In Fulfilment, Heb. 7. This might be Shem in type, Christ in antitype. Salem. Called, on the bricks of the ruins of an ancient city in S. of Palestine, Uru-Salim = the city of Salim. The Tablets show that Palestine was at this time in possession of Egypt, and the Tablets are letters to the Pharaohs Amenophis III and IV. One is from Ebed-Tob, the successor of Melchizedek. Three times he says "not my father, not my mother installed me in this place but the Mighty King" (cp. Heb. 7. 1-4), i.e. he did not inherit by succession, but by the gift and "the arm of the Mighty King" (the deity). wine. Same as 9. 20-24. See Ap. 27. i. priest. Yet no sacrifices. Hence a type of Him to Whom all shall bow (Ps. 110. 4), and pay their tithes and bring their gifts (Ps. 72). See note on 9. 27. MOST HIGH GOD. Heb. El Elyon, so vv. 19, 20, 22. See Ap. 4. First occ. of this title. Cp. 1st occ. in N.T. (Luke 1. 76) "Highest", in relation to the earth. See also Deut. 32. 8 (cp. Acts 17. 26). Ps. 8; 9. 18, 27; and note on Num. 24. 16.
he. Fig. Ellipsis = Abram (see Ap. 6). him = Melchizedek.
persons = Heb. nephesh, souls. Ap. 13. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part). See Ap. 6.
lift up mine hand = I swear. Cp. Ex. 6. 8. Ps. 106. 26. Isa. 3. 7 margin. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct). See Ap. 6.
I will not take. The blessing of Melchizedek, and the bread and wine, prepared him for this great renunciation.

15. 1-21 (G e1, p. 18). THE COVENANT MADE. The Seed and The Land. [For Structure see next page.] the word of the LORD. First occ. of this expression is with the prep. 'el, unto, implying action of a person; or, at least, articulate speech. a vision = the vision. Occurs only 4 times (here, Num. 24. 4, 16; Ezek. 13. 7). I am thy shield. Manifested in 14. 13-16 and 17-24. Cp. John 8. 56. The Incarnate Christ is Faith's shield (Eph. 6. 16).
Lord GOD. Heb. Adonai Jehovah. See Ap. 4. First occ., relating to blessing in the earth. go = am going on.
Behold ... lo. Fig. Asterismos (Ap. 6). heir. Heb. inherits me. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject). See Ap. 6. This was strictly in accordance with § 191 of the Code of Khammurabi. See Ap. 15.
Look. See note on 13. 14. now = steadfastly. stars. See on 13. 16 = the heavenly calling in Israel (Heb. 3. 1; 11. 9-16). Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. number them. Hence Joab's objection in 2 Sam. 24. 3.

believed: i.e. believed Jehovah = believed what he "heard" (Rom. 10. 17). counted = reckoned or imputed. righteousness. No art. = as righteousness. This was positive imputed righteousness (because he believed concerning Christ). It was more than forensic righteousness, which was negative or non-imputation of sin (Ps. 32. 1, 2). This was the consequence of the Gospel preached to Abram. (Cp. Gal. 3. 8, and read Rom. 4 and Gal. 3).
Lord GOD. Heb. Adonai Jehovah. See v. 2 and Ap. 4.
Take me = take for me: i.e. an offering for me. heifer. See Ap. 15.
these. Five, the No. of Grace, because Covenant was unconditional. See Ap. 10. divided. So Covenants were made (Jer. 34. 18-20). midst, i.e. in half.

Abram. Put to sleep so that he should have no part in it, and that the Covenant should be unconditional, in which "God was the one" and only contracting party (Gal. 3. 20). Cp. v. 17. Contrast "both", ch. 21. 27. lo. Fig. Asterismos. See Ap. 6.

Know of a surety. Heb. knowing thou shalt know. Fig. Polyptoton. See Ap. 6, and note on 26. 28. thy seed, i.e. Isaac. See note on 21. 12. The 400 years date from Isaac's birth (Acts 7. 6). The 430 from the "promise" or Covenant here made (cp. Gal. 3. 17), and include the whole "sojourning" (Ex. 12. 40). and shall serve, &c. Fig. Epitrechon. See Ap. 6. This is shown by the Structure (Introversion). a | Thy seed shall be a stranger, &c. / b | and shall serve them / b | and they shall afflict them / a | four hundred years. In a and a we have the whole sojourning and duration. In b and b the servitude in Egypt (215 years).
judge. Put by Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, for punish.
go to thy fathers = die and be buried. Abram's fathers were idolaters. Josh. 24. 2. Fig. Euphemism (Ap. 6).

fourth. Levi, Kohath, Amram, Moses; (or Levi), Jochebed (born in Egypt). iniquity. Heb. 'avon. See Ap. 44. iii. not yet. Another mark of the corruption of the Canaanite nations through the Nephilim and Rephaim.

behold. Fig. Asterismos. See Ap. 6. furnace. Symbolic of the affliction of Israel (Deut. 4. 20. 1 Kings 8. 51. Isa. 31. 9. Ezek. 22. 18-22. Jer. 11. 4). lamp. Symbolic of Israel's deliverance (1 Kings 11. 36; 15. 4. Isa. 62. 1. 2 Sam. 21. 17).
the LORD. Not Abram (Gal. 3. 17). See note on v. 12. have. Before this it was "I will". From now it is "I have". this land. Never yet possessed with these boundaries.
19, 20, 21 Ten nations. See Ap. 10.
Hittites. First occ. See Ex. 32. 2. Josh. 3. 10, &c. Rephaim. Another link in the chain from 6. 4. Cp. 12. 6; 13. 7; 14. 5; and see Ap. 23, 25.
handmaid. Not necessarily a slave. Cp. 1 Sam. 25. 41. Hagar = Heb. Flight. See v. 3.
ten. These 10 years to be taken into account in any calculations. wife. This was strictly in accordance with the enactment of Khammurabi (§ 146) which Abram had brought from Ur. See Ap. 15.
thee. Should be "her". See Ap. 31.
dealt hardly. Heb. afflicted her. The Code of Khammurabi (§ 119) forbade her being sold. Sarah could only lay tasks on her. See Ap. 15.

angel of the LORD. First occ. = messenger = 2nd Person, as being sent. Elohim = as being commissioned by oath. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. Shur = wall. The nearest way to her native land. Shur was the name of the great fortified wall shutting Egypt off from Palestine, with its Migdol or Fort.
face = presence. Fig. Pleonasm. See Ap. 6.

against. True to-day and for over 3,000 years. Cp. 21. 20. Isa. 21. 13. Jer. 3. 2. Ezra 8. 31. Ps. 10. 8, 9. presence = face, i.e. on the face of the same country. brethren. Esp. with the Midianites (37. 28), Midian being his half-brother, by Keturah (cp. Judg. 8. 22, 24). Cp. the fulfilment in 25. 18.

GOD. Heb. 'el. See Ap. 4. said. Translate: "Do I see, here, even after the Vision?" i.e. "Do I live, after seeing God?" looked = Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), implying living as well as looking. Cp. 32. 30. Judg. 13. 22.
Beer-lahai-roi = the well of living after seeing.

Hagar bare. Through infirmity of Sarah's faith. So the Law (parenthetically) "because of transgression" (Gal. 3. 19). Levitical Law given, as Ishmael was, until Christ the antitype of Isaac should be born (Gal. 4. 1-5, 19, 31).

the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. Almighty GOD = El Shaddai. First occ. See Ap. 4. This title assures Abram that He Who had called him was almighty to supply all his need. Cp. first occ. in N.T. (2 Cor. 6. 18), which assures us of the same supply. walk = continue to walk.
exceedingly. Fig. Epizeuxis (greatly greatly). Ap. 6.

fell. Cp. Mary (John 11. 32) and contrast Martha (John 11. 21). God = Elohim, Creator. Used in this ch. (vv. 3, 9, 15, 18, 22, 23) because He creates new names (vv. 5, 15), a new Sign of Covenant (vv. 9-14), and a new thing, from one as good as dead (Heb. 11. 12).
many. Emph. Fig. Antimereia (of Noun), for emphasis. Ap. 6.
Abraham. The fifth letter of Heb. alphabet (ה = H), put in middle of his name = No. 5, Grace. See Ap. 10. Abram = exalted father; Abraham = father of a multitude.
exceeding. Fig. Epizeuxis (greatly greatly). Ap. 6. nations. Abraham was the progenitor not only of Israel, but of Ishmaelites, Midianites, Arabians, &c.

covenant: unconditional. thy seed. Here, the coll. noun zer'a is shown to be plural by the words "after thee" (cp. vv. 8, 9), and by the pl. pron. "their generations" (vv. 7, 9). This is not the verse referred to in Gal. 3. 16, but Gen. 21. 12. See note on 21. 12, where "seed" must be in the sing. because of the verb. everlasting. Hence Israel so called. Isa. 44. 7 margin.
land ... stranger. Heb. land of thy sojournings.
thy seed. Still practised by Ishmaelites and others. Non-circumcision was the "reproach" of Egypt (Josh. 5. 9).
eight = the number of Resurrection (Ap. 10); associated here with circumcision, the sign of death.
flesh. Fig. Synecdoche, for the whole person. Ap. 6.
soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. Fig. Synecdoche, for person. Ap. 6.

Sarah. The addition of the 5th letter (ה = H) of Heb. alphabet (the No. of Grace, Ap. 10) as in Abraham's case (v. 5) and Joshua's (Num. 13. 16). The letter ה (H) is common to both the names of Jehovah and Elohim. Sarai = princely; Sarah = princess.
kings. Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., and Syr. read "and kings".

laughed: for joy. Heb. was joyful. Cp. John 8. 56, "rejoiced to see my day ... and was glad." The laughter of faith, Rom. 4. 19. Sarah did not fall down as Abraham did, v. 3. Shall, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. (Cp. Heb. 11. 12).
might live, as though he thought Ishmael was to die: showing his faith in Isaac's birth. This is proved from v. 20.
and. Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., Syr. read this "and" in the text.
I have heard. Showing the subject of Abraham's prayer. exceedingly. Fig. Epizeuxis (greatly greatly). Ap. 6.
Isaac. Heb. laughter. set time. See note on 1. 14.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. See Ap. 14. circumcised. Hence Ishmaelites and kindred nations still practise the rite.
thirteen. Symbolic; and in contrast with Isaac on eighth day. See Ap. 10. Ishmaelites and Arabians still circumcise in the 13th year.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. plains = among the oaks of Mamre. Cp. 13. 18; 14. 13; and 18. 8. sat = was sitting.

looked. See note on 13. 14. lo. The Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. three men. Elohim (Ap. 4) and two angels called men (Heb. 'ish, pl., Ap. 14) here, and vv. 16, 22: but in 19. 1, 15 the two are called "angels". Three the No. of Divine perfection (see Ap. 10). When two departed, Elohim (the Divine Presence) remained (vv. 16, 22).
LORD = Jehovah, not Adonai. See Ap. 32. But plural throughout ch. 19 of the two.
wash your feet. A common practice to this day; needed from use of sandals and bare feet; cp. 24. 32; 43. 24.
bread. Fig. Synecdoche (of Species), Ap. 6, put for food in general.
three measures. Note the No. 3. See v. 2 and Ap. 10. cakes. Evidently unleavened.
ran. Such speedy hospitality common in the East.
tree. See v. 1. eat. We do not understand this mystery. But we read of "angels' food" (Ps. 78. 25); and that Christ ate after His resurrection (Luke 24. 30, 43. Acts 10. 41).
Where, &c. Translate "And as to Sarah thy wife ... and he [interrupting] said, Lo! [she is] in the tent". See Ap. 31.
certainly return. Fig. Polyptoton (returning I will return) for emphasis. Ap. 6 and note on 26. 28. lo! Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. heard. Heb. was listening.
old. This explains how Rebekah, a grand-daughter of Abraham's brother, should be old enough to marry Isaac, Abraham's son.
laughed. See note on 17. 17. After. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. my lord. Heb. Adon. See Ap. 4 and cp. 1 Pet. 3. 6.
Wherefore? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
Is any thing? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. hard = wonderful. A similar question and same Fig. used in Luke 1. 37. time appointed. See note on 1. 14.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. See Ap. 14. looked = looked down upon. Heb. shakaph. 1st occ.
Shall I hide? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. Cp. Amos 3. 7.
shall surely become. Heb. "being shall be". Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6). See note on 26. 28. nations. Another proof that the mystery (Eph. 3) means more than Gentile blessing. Cp. 22. 18.
that = how that. command. Cp. Ps. 78. 1-8.
cry. Fig. Prosopopoeia. Ap. 6.

I will go down = let us now go down. See Gen. 11. 7. Ex. 3. 8, all times of judgment. the cry. Should be their outcry: with Sept., Onk., and ancient reading in MSS. called Sevir. See Ap. 34. I will know. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6.
the men. Prob. the two of 19. 1. Abraham stood yet before the LORD. The primitive text read "Jehovah stood yet before Abraham." One of the 18 emendations of the Sopherim. See Ap. 33.
also = even, or really. Note the 6 petitions in Abraham's prayer, vv. 24-32. See Ap. 10. wicked. Heb. rasha'. Ap. 44. x.
Peradventure = perhaps.
earth. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject). Ap. 6. "Earth" put for its inhabitants.

LORD*. One of the 134 places where the Primitive Text was Jehovah, and the Sopherim changed it to Adonai. These are distinguished in the text by an asterisk, and printed LORD*. See list, Ap. 32. dust and ashes. Fig. Meiosis. Ap. 6. Also Paronomasia (v'ephar 'aphar). Ap. 6. dust. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6.
went His way. The same as the one who came in vv. 1, 2.

two. Heb. the two. With art., viz. two of the three, 18. 16. Sodom = flaming, burning. even. Note emph. on notes of time in the Structure. gate. The seat of judgment, showing that Lot was a real citizen, v. 9; 23. 10, 18; 34. 20, 24. Ruth 4. 1.
my lords. Pl. of Adon. See Ap. 4. in the street. Fig. Peristasis. Ap. 6.
eat. See 18. 8.
men. Heb. pl. of 'enosh. Ap. 14. iii.
know. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6.
wickedly. Heb. ra'. Ap. 44. viii.
known. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. these. Archaic pron. showing antiquity of Pent. roof. Fig. Metalepsis. Ap. 6. Roof put for house, and house put for protection.
judge. See v. 1. He sat in Sodom's gate, the seat of the judges. See note on 13. 7. worse. Heb. ra'. Ap. 44. viii. break = break open, shiver.

blindness. Produced by dazzlings of light. Fig. Heterosis (of Noun). Ap. 6. Pl. put for sing. only here and 2 Kings 6. 18. 9 instances of people so smitten (see Ap. 10). See 19. 11; 27. 1; 48. 10. Judg. 16. 21. 1 Sam. 4. 15. 1 Kings 14. 4. 2 Kings 6. 18; 25. 7. Acts 13. 11.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton. Ap. 6.
will destroy = are about to destroy. face. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6.

the LORD. Cp. the "we" of v. 13. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. one that mocked = talked nonsense. He had looked, and pitched his tent toward Sodom, had dwelt and made his home there, and married his daughters, and sat in its gate as a judge. No wonder he seemed as one that mocked. He chose Sodom (13. 11), and "lingered" in the place of his choice (v. 16). See note, 13. 7.
iniquity. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. Cause put for effect = judgment. Cp. Ps. 7. 16. See Ap. 44. iii.
lingered. See v. 14.
He. Sept. reads "they". life = soul. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13. look, &c. Fig. Asyndeton. Ap. 6. (No ands, but climax.)
LORD*. See note on 18. 27.
is it not a little one? Fig. Epitrechon. Ap. 6. my soul = myself. Heb. my nephesh. Ap. 13.
thee. Heb. thy face. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part). Ap. 6. also. Omitted in A.V. 1611.
Zoar = little, or smallness. Cp. 14. 2, 8.

the LORD ... from the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Repetition very emphatic. Cp. "we", v. 13. brimstone and fire. Fig. Hendiadys (Ap. 6) = burning brimstone. Referred to in Deut. 29. 23. Isa. 13. 19. Jer. 49. 18. Zeph. 2. 9. Matt. 10. 15. 2 Pet. 2. 6. Jude 7.

overthrew. These cities are not in the Dead Sea, but their ruins have been discovered by M. de Saulcy (called to-day Kharbet-Goumran), about 4 miles square (Journey round the Dead Sea, vol. ii, pp. 42-46). Note the parallelism (Alternation). a | cities. / b | plain. / a | cities (inhabitants). / b | plain (produce).
wife. Cp. Luke 17. 32. looked back: i.e. curiously. Cp. Isa. 63. 5 and v. 28. Same word as in v. 17. became. Same word as 1. 2, "the earth became."
stood. Cp. note on 18. 22.
looked toward. A different word from v. 27. Abraham bent forward and looked with awe and grief. lo. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. smoke. It does not say he saw the cities, but only the smoke.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. remembered. Lot's deliverance due to Abraham's prayer. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. cities = the city. Fig. Heterosis (of Number). Ap. 6.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
wine. Heb. yayin. See Ap. 27. i.
33, 35 nor = but. This clause is one marked with the "fifteen extraordinary points" calling attention to the ancient reading = "he did know when she arose." See Ap. 31.
Moab. Heb. from a father.

Ben-ammi. Heb. son of Ammi = "the god Am". See on 14. 5 and Deut. 2. 20. Begotten in shame, both had a shameful history. Deut. 23. 3, 4. Cp. Judg. 10. 10; 11. 4, 15. Num. 21. 29. Deut. 2. 19; 3. 16. 2 Chron. 20. 1. Zeph. 2. 8.
south = the Negeb. See 12. 9; 13. 1.

said. Abraham's expedient = the next assault on Abraham in the Great Conflict for the destruction of the promised seed of the woman (Gen. 3. 15). See Ap. 23. God had to intervene (v. 3), for man could know nothing of it. Abraham's fear shown in v. 11. my sister = half-sister. See note on v. 12 and Ap. 29. Abimelech. Heb. Father-king. The official title of the kings of Gerar (cp. 26. 1), like Pharaoh in Egypt. took. See note on 21. 7. In Sarah's conception God must have renewed her youth, for she nursed Isaac (21. 7).

dream. 20 recorded in Scripture (see Ap. 10). 20. 3; 28. 12; 31. 10, 24; 37. 5, 9; 40. 5, 5; 41. 1, 5, 5. Judg. 7. 13. 1 Kings 3. 5. Dan. 2. 3; 4. 5; 7. 1. Matt. 1. 20; 2. 12, 13, 19; 27. 19. Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. man ... for. Fig. Aposiopesis, or "sudden silence". Ap. 6. We must supply "If thou dost not restore her"; or "I will slay thee". See vv. 4 and 7.
LORD* = Jehovah. One of the 134 emendations of the Sopherim. See Ap. 32. also, i.e. as well as Sodom and Gomorrah, ch. 19. nation. Abimelech evidently expected God to slay the whole nation.
I also withheld. Divine intervention needed. Cp. v. 2. Note the emphatic pronouns. See Ap. 23. sinning. See Ap. 44. i.

man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii. prophet. First occ., showing that prediction is only a small part of its meaning = God's spokesman. Here, it is prayer (cp. Ex. 4. 16 and 7. 1), and prayer is associated with prophesying, i.e. witnessing (1 Cor. 11. 5).
men. Heb. pl. of 'enosh. Ap. 14. iii.
What. Fig. Aganactesis. Ap. 6. sin. Heb. chat'a. See Ap. 44. i.
sawest thou = hadst thou seen.
thought. Heb. said: i.e. said [to myself]. slay me. Showing how his fears were worked upon by the enemy. See v. 2.
sister. The daughter of Terah by another wife (than Abraham's mother): therefore, Abraham's half-sister. See Ap. 29.
caused. The verb is in the plural. kindness. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. Kindness put for the kind deeds caused by it.
and. Fig. Polysyndeton. Ap. 6.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.

brother. Fig. Irony. Ap. 6. covering, &c. Fig. Periphrasis. Ap. 6. Having called Abraham her "brother", he uses this beautiful Figure for her husband. Cp. 24. 65. 1 Cor. 11. 5, &c. reproved, i.e. by the Irony.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. as = according as. said. Emphasis on "said" for our faith. spoken. Fig. Pleonasm (Ap. 6), for emphasis.

set time = exact time. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. Note change of title here, till v. 32, because it is Creator and creature. In v. 33, Jehovah, where it is Covenant relation. In Mary's song both titles united (Luke 1. 46, 47 and cp. vv. 37, 38).
eight. The Dominical No. See Ap. 10. Cp. Ishmael, 13th year.
hundred. See Ap. 10.

suck. A proof that "God", the Creator, had renewed her youth, showing why Abimelech should have taken her (20. 2). Sarah's Magnificat may be compared with Mary's. The scenes of both near to each other. Mary's words (Luke 1. 54, 55) connect her "mercy" with that shown to "Abraham and his seed".
grew. Cp. Luke 2. 40.
mocking. Heb. "laughing" or "chaffing", or "mocking again" (as we say).
Cast out, &c. See the Divine interpretation. Gal. 3. 6-29; 4. 22-31; 5. 1-12. with my son, &c. Heb. idiom "with my son—with Isaac". Cp. Num. 12. 8.
thing. Heb. word.

Isaac ... thy seed. Here zer'a is in the sing. sense, because of the word "Isaac", and because of the sing. verb "it shall be called." Zer'a is a collective noun (like Eng. "sheep"), but the context must determine whether it is sing. or pl. It is to this verse Gal. 3. 16 refers; not to 12. 7, where it is indefinite; or 17. 7 where the verb and pronouns show it is plural. See note there, and on Gal. 3. 16; and cp. Rom. 9. 7. Heb. 11. 18. "Thy seed" is therefore "Christ". The difference of the 30 years comes in here: 430 to the Exodus (12. 40) from Gen. 12. 4, when Abraham was 75: 25 thence to Isaac's birth: and now, 5 to his recognition as the seed = 30 years.
bottle. Cp. man's provision (a bottle) with God's (a well) (v. 19).
as it were, &c. Fig. Epitheton. Ap. 6. not see, &c. Fig. Tapeinosis. Ap. 6. lift up her voice = the boy lifted up his voice and wept. So Sept. (see v. 17).
heard. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. What, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. heard. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6.
well. Heb. b'er, a well (digged): not 'ayin, a spring or fountain; or bor, a cistern (hewn).
kindness. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. See 20. 13.
violently, &c. Cp. 26. 19, 20. Ex. 2. 17. Judg. 5. 11. This explains Ex. 17. 8, "Then came Amalek", because of vv. 1-7.
wot not = know not. O. Eng. idiom.
both. Not one party as in 15. 10-18. Cp. Gal. 3. 20. made. Heb. cut, because of the dividing of the sacrifice. Cp. 15. 10. Jer. 34. 18-20. Eng. concluded or solemnised.
Beer-sheba = Heb. well of the oath.

grove. Heb. 'eshel = trees, not 'asherah (Ap. 42), but the wood for 22. 3 about twenty years later. the everlasting GOD. This is the Divine definition of Jehovah (LORD), Heb. 'olam = duration, secret and hidden from man. Cp. Ps. 90. 2.

God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. after, i.e. after 40 or 50 years in Canaan. tempt. Heb. prove, so Ex. 15. 25; 16. 4; 20. 20. Deut. 8. 2, 16. Judg. 2. 22; 3. 1, 4. Ecc. 2. 1; 7. 23. 1 Sam. 17. 39. 1 Kings 10. 1. 2 Chron. 9. 1; 33. 31. Ps. 26. 2. Cp. Deut. 4. 34 (assayed). In later usage trial meant trouble. Wisd. 3. 5; 11. 10. Sir. 2. 1. Judith 8. 24-27. Luke 8. 13 (cp. Matt. 13. 21). Acts 20. 19. Heb. 2. 18. 1 Pet. 1. 6. Behold, &c. = behold me.

lovest. Note the reference to the Antitype. Moriah. Heb. = shown or provided by Jah. Cp. 1 Chron. 21. 22; 22. 1. 2 Chron. 3. 1. Christ crucified also on one of these mountains. Matt. 27. 33. offer. Heb. 'alah. See Ap. 43. I. vi. burnt offering. Heb. 'olah. See Ap. 43. II. ii.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), emphasising the calmness of Abraham's deliberate faith. Each "and" is to be noted, and each act weighed.
the third day. No. 3. Symb. of resurrection (Ap. 10). Cp. v. 5, "Come again," 1st pers. pl. Exactly 3 days journey from Beer-sheba to Moriah. Gerizim is 2 days' further.

I and the lad. This is polite Hebrew, while "the lad and I" would be polite English. yonder. Heb. as far as there (as though pointing). come again. This was proof of Abraham's faith. 1st pers. plural, "We will come again."

laid. Cp. John 19. 17. fire. Without doubt fire from Abraham's own altar (12. 7; 13. 4, 18; and see note on 21. 33), for God accepted a sacrifice only by fire from heaven. See on 4. 4. both of them together. Cp. the Father and the Son in the antitype. Emph. by repetition in v. 8. John 10. 30; 14. 10, 11; 16. 33. The sinner is not seen in the type; his part is subsequent to this, viz. to believe what the Father and the Son have done for him in substitution. See also Rom. 8. 32. 2 Cor. 5. 19.
Here, &c. Heb. Behold me, my son.
provide. Heb. yireh = God will see or look out. Himself = for Himself. a lamb. Heb. the lamb.
9, 10 and. Each act is emph. by the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), and is to be dwelt upon and considered. an altar. Heb. the altar.

the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. Abraham, Abraham. Fig. Epizeuxis (Ap. 6), for emph. Cp. the 10 Duplications: (1) Seven used by God to men: 22. 11; 46. 2. Ex. 3. 4. 1 Sam. 3. 10. Luke 10. 41; 22. 31. Acts 9. 4; (2) Three under other circumstances: Matt. 7. 21, 22 (Luke 6. 46; 13. 25). Matt. 23. 37 (Luke 13. 34). Mark 15. 34 (Matt. 27. 46. Ps. 22. 1).
now I know. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6.

lifted up his eyes. Fig. Pleonasm, for emph. (Ap. 6). looked. See note on 13. 14. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. a ram. Some Cod. (with Sam., Jon., Sept., and Syr.) read "one ram", i.e. a solitary ram. a thicket. Heb. the thicket. in the stead. Here is the doctrine of substitution, clearly stated.

Jehovah-jireh. Heb. Jehovah will see, or provide, as in v. 8. See Ap. 4. In the mount, &c. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. it shall be seen: it will be provided, or "in the mount Jehovah will be seen". So it was in 2 Sam. 24. 25. 1 Chron. 21. 26. 2 Chron. 7. 1-3.
the second time. Heb. a second time; the first time was for substitution; the second was for revelation.
sworn. This oath is the foundation of Israel's blessings (24. 7; 26. 3; 50. 24. Ex. 13. 5, 11; 33. 1). David's "sure mercies" all grounded on it (Ps. 89. 35; 132. 11. Cp. Luke 1. 73).

blessing I will bless = I will surely bless; or, I will richly bless. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis. stars ... sand, &c. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. See note on 13. 16. the gate. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6. "Gate" put for the cities.
all the nations. Proof that the "Mystery" does not mean blessing of Gentiles as such: but the secret concerning Christ and the church (Eph. 5. 32).

22. 20-24 (B1, p. 17). THE POSTERITY OF NAHOR. Introduced here to lead up to Rebekah, the future wife of Isaac. Not proceeding further with Nahor's posterity. See (p. 17) how Abraham's history is broken up into three portions by two posterities, just as Isaac's and Jacob's histories are broken up. See p. 52, and Ap. 29.
these eight. Nahor had 12 in all, as Ishmael had (25. 13-16), and as Jacob had (35. 23-27).
Maachah. See Deut. 3. 14. Josh. 12. 5. 2 Sam. 10. 6.

23. 1—24. 67 (A2, p. 17). ABRAHAM'S HISTORY. (OLD AGE.) [For Structure see next page.] Sarah. The only woman whose age is mentioned in the Bible. In 22. 23 Rebekah is mentioned: one sun rising before the other sets.
Kirjath-arba. See notes on Num. 13. 22, and Ap. 25. Hebron. See note on Num. 13. 22.
before his dead. Heb. leaning over the face of his dead. Fig. Pleonasm. Ap. 6.
I am. Cp. "thou art", v. 6. stranger and a sojourner. Cp. 1 Pet. 2. 11. Ps. 39. 12.
children. Heb. sons, and so elsewhere.
mighty prince. Heb. prince of El. Gen. of relation (Ap. 17), for Adjective. Cp. Ps. 36. 7; 80. 10.
mind = soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.
money. Heb. silver. buryingplace. What Jacob bought (33. 19, 20) was for an altar.
dwelt. Heb. was sitting there.
give I. Heb. have I given. Fig. Antimereia (of Verb), past for present, Ap. 6.
wilt give. Fig. Ellipsis. Ap. 6. Supply "hast given" from v. 11.
what is that. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
Abraham. This is not the purchase referred to in 33. 19 and Acts 7. 16. 80 years between this purchase and Jacob's. See note on Acts 7. 16. before all. Some Cod. with Sam. have "even before all".

made sure. This was all strictly in conformity with the commercial enactments of the Code of Khammurabi. See Ap. 15. buryingplace. All that Abraham possessed; but in the faith and hope of resurrection.
24 (X2, above). THE MARRIAGE OF ISAAC. [For Structure see next page.] old. About 140 years old. the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.

eldest servant. Prob. Eleazar of Damascus. 15. 2. thigh. According to the Midrash and ancient Jewish expositors, a Euphemism (Ap. 6) for the organs of generation, as most sacred. According to Ibn Ezra and present Indian custom, on the thigh is a token of subjection.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. Canaanites. Mixed with the Nephilim. Ap. 23, 25. I. Emph. in contrast with the Canaanites. Hence Abraham's horror of mixing the holy seed with that of the Nephilim.
my kindred. Gentiles thus expressly excluded from this chapter, if regarded as a type. Cp. vv. 3, 4, 7, 37, 38. See also 26. 35; 27. 46; 28. 1, 8.
thither. Cp. Heb. 11. 15.

heaven. The Sept. reads: "heaven, and God of the earth." See Ap. 4. father's house, and from the land of my kindred. The Severus Codex reads: "from my house and from my country," as in v. 4. See Ap. 34.
arose = mounted. Mesopotamia. Heb. Aram-naharaim, i.e. Aram of the two rivers (the Tigris and Euphrates). The country of Haran. 11. 31.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. well = spring. Heb. 'ayin. See note on 21. 19. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. come out. Heb. are coming out.
pitcher. Still used in Palestine as in John 4. 28. I will give. A sign requested contrary to the custom. Cp. 29. 10.
before he had done speaking. Cp. Isa. 65. 24. Rebekah. Heb. captivating. born to Bethuel. See Ap. 29. Bethuel. Heb. separated of God.
virgin. Heb. bethulah. Cp. v. 43. See note on v. 43. man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
wondering: or eagerly watching her. to wit = to know.
golden. Heb. of gold. Gen. of material. Ap. 17. earring. Prob. a nose (or "face") ring. See v. 47.
Nahor. See Ap. 29. Rebekah his granddaughter; but old enough to marry Isaac, because Sarah was "well stricken in years" when Isaac was born (18. 11, 12). Cp. 24. 36.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
Laban. See Ap. 29.
when he saw. Characteristic of Laban. Rebekah showed kindness before she saw.
31, 32 he, i.e. Laban.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14.
And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton, Ap. 6, to emphasise all the items which went to make up Abraham's wealth. Twelve "ands" (3 x 4 = 12) = abundance of earthly wealth. See Ap. 10.
I walk = I walk habitually. Heb. verb in Hithpael.

said. Eleazar repeats his prayer from memory, but inexactly. Who could have written the actual words (vv. 12-21) but the Holy Inspiring Spirit? He records both the prayer itself and Eleazar's remembrance of it.

virgin. Heb. 'almah. Every bethulah is an 'almah, but every 'almah is not a bethulah: 'almah occ. 7 times, 24. 43 (first occ.). Ex. 2. 8. Ps. 68. 25. Prov. 30. 19. Song, 1. 3; 6. 8. Isa. 7. 14. Bethulah occ. 49 times (Ap. 10).
face or nose. Cp. v. 22.
led me in the right way. Cp. Ps. 107. 7. daughter. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Species), Ap. 6, daughter put for granddaughter.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. as the LORD hath spoken = according as Jehovah, &c. Laban regards Jehovah as arranging all.
raiment: or garments; i.e. changes of raiment.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. Ap. 14. iii.
ten. Seven days = a week, but ten or a decad (1/3 of a month) sometimes reckoned as a longer, but strictly defined period. Cp. Ex. 12. 3. Lev. 16. 29.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
well = spring. Heb. b'er. See note on 21. 19. Lahai-roi. Heb. the well of life and vision.

meditate. Refers back to the historical context, 23. 19, the death and burial of Sarah, his mother. What follows this digression (of which Isaac as yet knew nothing) in 24. 1-67 shows that Isaac went out, not to "meditate", or "to pray" (A.V. marg.), or "take a walk" (Syr.), or "muster the flocks" (Gesenius), but to mourn. This is the meaning of the Heb. suach in Ps. 44. 25. Lam. 3. 20. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
lighted off. Heb. fell, or alighted hastily.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
comforted after, or consoled himself for.

25. 1-4 (B2, p. 17). THE POSTERITY OF KETURAH. This genealogy, and Abraham's death recorded here, because no more is to be said about Abraham. Abraham, however, lived till Jacob was 15. Shem died 1846. a wife = another, instead of "again".
Medan and Midian were half-brothers with Ishmael, and they were mixed up together in their dealings. See note on 37. 25, 28, and cp. 16. 12; 17. 20.
these = the tares, sown after Isaac, the good seed.
175 years. Therefore a sojourner 100 years. Cp. 12. 4.

full of. Heb. "satisfied with". Supply "days" (not "years"), with Sam., Onk., Jon., Sept., and Syr. gathered to his people, an idiomatic Euphemism (Ap. 6) for death and burial. Abraham's "people" were idolaters (Josh. 24. 2). See note on 2 Sam. 12. 23.
Machpelah. Cp. 23. 9.
purchased. Cp. 23. 16.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. well. Heb. b'er. See note on 21. 19. Lahai-roi. Cp. 16. 14; 24. 62.

died = had inheritance. Heb. naphal, to fall, esp. as a lot, giving inheritance (Judg. 18. 1. 1 Chron. [illegible]; 26. 14. 2 Chron. 15. 9. Ps. 16. 6 (cp. Josh. 23. 4. Heb. caused the lot to fall). Hence, to dwell with, as in Prov. 1. 14. Cp. Judg. 7. 12, to encamp, lying along the ground. Ishmael was to dwell in the presence (Heb. "on the face") of his brethren, i.e. mixed up with them (16. 12). See 37. 25, 28, 36; 39. 1, and cp. Judg. 8. 24 (Midian, being his half-brother (15. 11, 12). Naphal never rendered "die" elsewhere.
begat. The same form of the verb as in ch. 5, used of the godly seed.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
heel. Heb. yakob, whence the name Jacob (yakob) heel-catcher: hence, contender.
cunning = knowing or skilled in. a man of the field. "The field is the world." plain = upright or pure. Job 1. 1, 8; 2. 3, &c.

venison. Heb. hunting. Fig. Metonymy (of the Cause), Ap. 6, hunting put for what was caught. Eating was strong in Esau too (v. 34). It was "the will of the flesh" which Isaac's faith overcame in ch. 27, for he wished to bless Esau, and he loved his savoury meat. See note on 27. 3, 4. Cp. Heb. 11. 20.
sod. Part. of O. Eng. verb seethe, to boil. pottage = anything cooked in a pot.
red. Heb. red red. Fig. Epizeuxis (Ap. 6). (No superlative in Heb.) Fig. = that delicious red [food]. Lentiles. See v. 34. Edom = Heb. red, ruddy. A reference also to v. 25.

this day. Heb. "as on this very day." Fig. Simile. Ap. 6. Cp. Luke 23. 43. birthright. Included (1) the Father's blessing and supremacy (which went to Jacob, ch. 27, and Judah, 49. 8. 1 Chron. 5. 1, 2); (2) a double portion (which went to Joseph, ch. 48. 1 Chron. 5. 1, 2); and (3) the Domestic Priesthood (which after going to the first-born of each family was vested in Levi for the whole nation, Num. 3. 6, 12. Cp. Num. 16. 1-3).
me. Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6) = Brachyology. The words to be supplied are "I will sell it". A famine accounts for the sale. See 26. 1.
day. Fig. Brachyology. Ap. 6. Supply "that thou wilt sell it". birthright. The Severus Codex here reads "ware", i.e. Esau treated his birthright as merchandise. See Ap. 34.

and. Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6). Four "ands" marking the deliberateness of Esau's acts, and their solemn significance. He despised grace. See Ap. 10. despised. Hence in Heb. 12. 16 he is called "a profane person".

26 (D E, p. 36). ISAAC'S JOURNEY TO GERAR. famine. Accounts for Esau's despair of living, and hence selling his birthright. 25. 29-34. first. One of the thirteen famines. See note on 12. 10. Abimelech = official name. Not the same as ch. 20. 2.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4. Go not down (as Abraham did, ch. 12. 10).
unto thee. So to each Patriarch: Abraham (13. 15), Jacob (28. 13, &c.), involving resurrection. See note on 50. 24, and cp. Ex. 3. 6 and Matt. 22. 23-33.
stars. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6.

My. Repeated 5 times for emph. The No. of Grace. See Ap. 10 and note on John 1. 17. voice, to be heard and believed (Rom. 10. 17). charge, to be observed. commandments, to be obeyed. statutes, i.e. decrees, to be acknowledged. laws, i.e. instructions to be followed.
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14. he said. As Abraham had said (12. 13; 20. 2, 12). sister. See note on 20. 12.
sporting with, or caressing.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. how ... ? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
What ... ? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. guiltiness. See Ap. 15 and 44. ii.
saying. One of the Laws given and observed before Moses. See Ap. 15.
received. Heb. found. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Species). Ap. 6. Cp. 6. 8. Rom. 4. 1.
store = body.
the valley. Some distance from the city.

in the days of Abraham his father. Isaac a placid character: shown by his obedience (22. 6, 8), his meekness in betrothal (24), his mourning for his mother (24. 63-67; cp. note on v. 63), his following in his father's steps to Gerar (20. 1) in denying his wife there (20), his finding an Abimelech and Phichol there, and digging wells there, renewing the oath and renaming the well. their names. Cp. the four names below and their special meaning.
well. Heb. 'ayin. See note on 21. 19. springing. Heb. living. See note on 21. 19.
Esek. Heb. strife or contention.
Sitnah. Heb. opposition.
Rehoboth. Heb. roominess.
Beer-sheba. Heb. the well of the oath.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
Phichol. Prob. an official military title. Cp. 21. 22.

saw certainly. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), for emphasis. Heb. "seeing we saw". Cp. 2. 16 "freely eat"; 27. 30 "scarce gone out"; 43. 3 "solemnly protest"; 43. 7 "asked us straitly", "could we certainly know"; 43. 20 "came indeed down"; Ex. 5. 23 "not delivered us at all"; 18. 18 "wilt surely wear away"; 21. 5 "shall plainly say"; Job 37. 2 "hear attentively"; Num. 22. 17, 37 "promote thee to very great honour" = honouring I will honour thee; 24. 10 "altogether blessed", Heb. "blessing thou hast blessed". Num. 26. 65; 30. 12 "utterly destroyed"; 23. 11; 24. 10 "altogether blessed".
touched. Fig. Tapeinosis. Ap. 6. Emphasising the fact that so far from injuring him in any way they had shown him favour.
Shebah. Heb. an oath. therefore. Same name given by Abraham (21. 31). Names were sometimes reimposed for a new reason. Cp. Bethel (28. 18, 19 with 35. 6, 7) and Israel (32. 28 with 35. 10).

These names exhibit the Fig. Polynymia. Ap. 6. Judith. She had a second name, Aholibamah (36. 5, 14, 25). Beeri. His name was also Anah, but he had acquired the name "Beeri" (or the spring-man) from his having discovered the hot springs. See on 36. 24. Hittite = the general name. See note on 1 Kings 10. 29. Bashemath had a second name, Adah. The name Bashemath dropped in 36. 2 to avoid confusion with the daughter of Ishmael. In ch. 26 we have general history, but in 36 precise genealogy.
grief. Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6, grief put for that which caused it. No wonder it caused "bitterness of spirit" when we remember who the Canaanites were. mind = spirit. Heb. ruach. See Ap. 9.
old. About 137 years (same age as his brother Ishmael died at). He recovered and lived 43 years longer (cp. 35. 28). Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.

take me some venison. Heb. hunt me some hunting. Fig. Polyptoton, Ap. 6, and Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, by which venison, the result of hunting, is put for the hunting itself (from Lat. venatio, a hunting). In ch. 25. 29 Esau missed his venison and lost his birthright. Was he now to miss it again and lose his blessing?

such as I love. See vv. 9, 14 and 25. 28. my soul = myself. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. bless thee. He must have heard that he was to bless Jacob, for it was "by faith" he ultimately did so (Heb. 11. 20); and it came "by hearing" (Rom. 10. 17). "The will of the flesh" made him wish to bless Esau (cp. v. 4 with 25. 28). But his faith in the end overcame "the will of the flesh" in him.
heard. Heb. was listening. spake. Heb. was speaking.
the LORD. Heb. Jehovah. Ap. 4.
man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.
seem. He shrinks, not from the fraud, but from its detection.

goodly. Heb. desires. Fig. Metonymy (of the Adjunct), Ap. 6, put for the things desired or coveted (2 Chron. 36. 10. Isa. 64. 11. Lam. 1. 10). raiment. All raiment in the East to this day marks the social rank and position of the wearer. Among the Bedouins, the chief and his eldest son wear a distinctive garment. This accounts for Jacob's desire here, and his act with Joseph (37. 3). Being the garment of the firstborn it doubtless denoted also his official and priestly position. Here, Heb. beged (cp. Ex. 28. 2, 4; 35. 19. Lev. 10. 6; 21. 10), used of sacred things. Not the word rendered clothes in Deut. 29. 5. No wonder Esau is called "profane" when he sold this his birthright (Heb. 12. 16).
I am. Said perhaps because he had bought the birthright. thy soul = thou. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
wine = Heb. yayin. See Ap. 27. i.

now. Not an adv. of time, but an expletive in command, emphasising the solemnity of the command. It must have been at this point that Isaac's faith overcame "the will of the flesh", and made him resolve to bless Jacob, in spite of it.

corn. Put by Metonymy (of the Cause), Ap. 6, for bread and solid food generally. Cp. Lam. 2. 12. wine. Heb. tirosh. See Ap. 27. ii. Usually combined with "corn", as put by Metonymy (of the Cause) for all liquids. Ap. 6.
people. Heb. peoples.
scarce gone out. Heb. "going was gone". Fig. Polyptoton, for emph.; well represented by the word "scarce". See note on 26. 28.
thy firstborn. Esau still claims what he had sold.

trembled very exceedingly. The Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6) is thus beautifully rendered. Heb. "trembled a great trembling greatly." See note on 26. 28. This trembling was not from doubt, or from the discovery (now made, vv. 26, 27), but on account of the difficulty into which it had brought him with a man of Esau's temperament.
Jacob. See on 25. 26. supplanted. Jacobed or over-reached me. See note on 25. 26 and 32. 28. blessing. This "blessing" is the "it" of Heb. 12. 17.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. thy lord = a mighty man unto thee. See Ap. 14. iv. Fulfilled in 2 Sam. 8. 14. wine. See note on v. 28 above.
wept. See Heb. 12. 17, but could not change his father's mind.

Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. the fatness of the earth, and of. Heb. of the fatness, &c. The "of", which is omitted in the first clause, is the prep. מ, which means "from". R.V. marg. away from. Cp. Isa. 22. 3. Jer. 48. 33. Lam. 4. 9. Should be "Far from the fatness of the earth shall be thy dwelling, and far from the dew of the heavens," &c. Jacob had already received the blessing "of" the fatness of the earth or the land (v. 28). Esau's was to be far from it, in the desert; and so it was.
serve. See 1 Sam. 14. 47. 2 Sam. 8. 14. 2 Kings 8. 20, and cp. 1 Kings 22. 47. thou shalt break. Fulfilled in 2 Kings 8. 20, 22. 2 Chron. 21. 8-10.
at hand. Isaac mistaken, vv. 1, 2. Esau mistaken here.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
flee thou. Heb. flee for thyself. Haran. See 11. 31.
a few days. Rebekah mistaken, for he was there 20 years. until. Fig. Synonymia. Ap. 6.
why ... ? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. both. Jacob by Esau's hand, and Esau by the avenger of blood. 9. 6.
daughters of Heth. Refers to Esau's wives. 26. 34, 35. what good. Fig. Erotesis, and Fig. Aposiopesis, Ap. 6. Lit. "Wherefore to me life?" Eng. Idiom, "What good would my life be to me?"
blessed. This blessing God endorses (vv. 13-15), by sending Jacob to Haran, as he had blessed Abraham to bring him from Haran (12. 1-3). Thou shalt not take. See 24. 3.
Padan-aram = the plain of Syria.

And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton in vv. 3 & 4 (Ap. 6), marking 4 items in blessing. See Ap. 10. GOD ALMIGHTY. El Shaddai. See Ap. 4. multitude: or convocation. Heb. kahal. First occ. Occurs 123 times: rendered "multitude" 3, "assembly" 17, "congregation" 86, "company" 17. Cp. 49. 6. Ps. 22. 22, 25. people. Heb. peoples.
wherein thou art a stranger. Heb. of thy sojournings. God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), emphasising (vv. 6-8) the effort of Esau to note what would please his parents. Canaan. Cp. 24. 3, and remember who these Canaanites were. See note on 12. 6.
pleased not. Cp. 26. 35.
Mahalath. She had a second name, Bashemath. See ch. 36. 3.
And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), emphasizing the items in vv. 10-15.
of the stones. Heb. from; i.e. one from among them. Cp. vv. 18, 22.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. ladder. Heb. sullam, from salal, to pile up like terraces; a way cast up, stairway. Occurs only here. Cp. Isa. 35. 8-10; 57. 14; 62. 10.

the LORD = Jehovah (Ap. 4). above it. The Heb. accent (zark'a) emphasizes this as meaning "beside him" (cp. 18. 2, where 'al is rendered "by"). It is not the angels, but the Divine faithfulness and promise, which mark "this place" (vv. 16, 17) and make it "the house of God". to thee. As He had said to Abraham (13. 15) and to Isaac (26. 3). See note on 50. 24. will I. Note the "shalls" and "wills" in this and all these repetitions of Jehovah's covenant.
dust ... &c. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. See on 15. 5. in thee. Mark the personal gift, and see note on 17. 7 and 50. 24. all. This can be fulfilled only in Christ.

I will not leave thee. This promise first made, here, to Jacob for covenant grace; to the People, for journey (Deut. 31. 6); to Joshua, for conflict (Josh. 1. 5, 8); to Solomon, for work (1 Chron. 28. 20); to us, for daily provision (Heb. 13. 5, 6).
Surely. Fig. Ecphonesis. Ap. 6. this place. See on the word "above", v. 13.

the house of God. This "house" is the place where God meets the unworthy in grace. It was so with David (1 Chron. 22. 1). It is so for us. Our "place of worship" is where God manifests Himself to us in grace. "The God of all grace" is emphatically "the God of Jacob" (Ps. 146. 5).

the stone. See v. 11. Not the so-called "Coronation stone" in London: inasmuch as the heads of the "Geological Survey of Great Britain" unanimously declared that "no stone of that kind was to be found in any part of the Holy Land whence it traditionally comes". Prof. Ramsay also pronounced it as being "not known to occur in Egypt or in the rocks around Bethel". pillar. Afterwards forbidden. Lev. 26. 1. Deut. 16. 22. poured oil. A law before Moses. See Ap. 15.
Beth-el. Heb. the house of El.
vowed a vow = made a solemn vow. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. The first recorded vow.
this stone. See vv. 11, 18. God's house. Heb. Beth-elohim, not Beth-el. tenth. See Ap. 15 and cp. 14. 20.
went, &c. = lifted up his feet. Heb. Idiom, Ap. 6.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. well. Heb. b'er. See note on 21. 19. three flocks. Cp. v. 8.
son. Fig. Synecdoche (of Species), Ap. 6, put for grandson. Cp. 24. 15. In v. 12 Jacob calls himself the "brother" of Laban by the same Fig.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
Lo. Fig. Asterismos, Ap. 6, giving life to the scene.
her father's sheep. Shepherds usually slaves, younger sons, or daughters. Cp. David, 1 Sam. 17. 13-15. Ex. 2. 16, 17. Note exception, Gen. 37. 14, and reason.
kissed. The Eastern greeting.
brother. See on v. 5 and Ap. 29.
heard the tidings. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. "Heard the hearing." and. Fig. Polysyndeton, Ap. 6, for emphasis.
space of a month. Heb. a month of days, i.e., by Fig. Hypallage (Ap. 6), the days of a month. Cp. Num. 11. 20.
Leah. Heb. weary. Rachel. Heb. a ewe.
tender = weak. beautiful = comely in form. Cp. 39. 6. well favoured = comely in countenance.
served. Cp. Hos. 12. 12.
Zilpah. See on v. 29.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. To call attention to the fact that he was deceived, as he had deceived Isaac (ch. 27).
we, i.e. I, by Fig. Heterosis (of Number). Ap. 6.

her, i.e. Leah's week. he gave him Rachel. A popular mistake to suppose that Jacob did not marry Rachel till the end of the second seven years, for in the first seven were born seven sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, and Joseph. In the second seven: Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulon, and Dinah.
Bilhah. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, § 145. See Ap. 15.

LORD. Jehovah used with the five sons (29. 31-35 and 30. 24). Elohim is used with six (30. 2, 6, 17, 18, 20, 23). No title used with Benjamin (35. 16-18). All were in pairs. Two pairs from Leah, one pair from Bilhah, one from Zilpah, one from Leah, one from Rachel. hated. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause), Ap. 6, by which love and hate are put for the esteem or neglect, caused by love and hate = less loved, Deut. 21. 15. Matt. 6. 24. Luke 14. 26.
Reuben. Heb. behold a son. For the various orders of the 12 tribes, see Ap. 45.
heard. Heb. sham'a (heard). Simeon. Heb. Shim'on (hearing). Fig. Paronomasia, Ap. 6.

joined. Heb. yillaveh (joined). was his name called. Heb. she called his name, with Sam. and Sept. Error due to neglected abbreviation in primitive Heb. text. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6. Levi. Heb. Levi (joiner).
praise. Heb. 'odeh (I shall, or, Let me praise); y'hudah (he shall be praised). Cp. Gen. 49. 8. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6. left: i.e. for a time.
children. Heb. sons.
God's. See note on 29. 31.
Bilhah. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, § 145. See Ap. 15. Cp. 29. 29. have children. Heb. be builded up. See note above, and cp. 16. 1-3.
judged. Heb. dananni (judged). Dan. Heb. judge. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6.

And. Fig. Polysyndeton, for emphasis. Ap. 6. great wrestlings have I wrestled. Heb. with wrestlings of El (= GOD) i.e. mighty wrestlings. Fig. Polyptoton, and Paronomasia. Ap. 6. Naphtali. Heb. my wrestling.
Zilpah ... wife. This was strictly in accordance with the Code of Khammurabi, § 145. Cp. 16. 1-3; 30. 3, 4. See Ap. 15.
A troop. Heb. over-run, or, have victory; so the Sept., Syr., Arab., Onk., Vulg. Gad = Jupiter (of the Babylonians). See Isa. 65. 11 marg., and Josh. 11. 17; 12. 7, where Baal-Gad = the God-Jupiter.
Happy. Heb. b'ashri (happy). will call, &c. Heb. 'ishshruni (sure to call me). Asher. Heb. Asher (happy). Cp. Deut. 33. 24. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6.
mandrakes. Sept. mandragora, the root easily formed, by pinching it, into the shape of a man. Hence its name; also supposed to be and used as a "love-philtre". Arab. = "apples of Satan".
hire. Heb. s'kari (hire). Fig. Paronomasia. (Ap. 6), with Issachar. Issachar. Heb. there is hire, or, he is wages.
dowry. God hath dowered me with a good dowry. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. Zebulun. Heb. dwelling, or habitation. An Assyrian word, to honour, brought out of Ur.
daughter. Jacob may have had other daughters not named. Dinah. Heb. prob. vindication, or, judgment.
God remembered. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. 22-24 Fig. Hysterologia, Ap. 6, for Joseph born after Naphtali, not after Dinah. This Fig. is used to keep Leah's children together.
Joseph. Heb. yoseph, may He add. The LORD. Note the occurrence of Jehovah here in connection with Joseph. shall add. Heb. yoseph, is adding. Fig. Paronomasia. Ap. 6.
tarry: for. Fig. Ellipsis, Ap. 6. ii d, which requires some such supply. experience by divination. Heb. nihashti, from nahash (Gen. 3. 1).
provide. Heb. the verb to do, which by Metonymy (of the Cause), Ap. 6, means to provide, or, do for. house. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject), Ap. 6, by which "house" is put for all who dwell in it.
answer. By the Fig. Prosopopoeia, Ap. 6, righteousness is personified. in time to come. Heb. to-morrow. Fig. Antimereia (of Adverb), Ap. 6 = some future day.
the man. Heb. ha-'ish. Ap. 14. ii. exceedingly. Heb. m'od m'od = greatly greatly. Fig. Epizeuxis. Ap. 6.
glory. Heb. weight. Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6 = wealth, the effect (i.e. the burden or weight) being put for that which caused it.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. as before. Heb. yesterday and the day before. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6 = aforetime.
the LORD = Jehovah (Ap. 4).
your father: repeated at beginning of next verse by the Fig. Anadiplosis. Ap. 6.
suffered him not. Fig. Idioma. Ap. 6. Heb. did not give him to do me evil. hurt. Heb. ra'a'. See Ap. 44. viii.
angel of God (Heb. Elohim). In v. 13 called by Himself, "I am the God of Beth-el", El of Beth-el. Cp. 28. 12, 13, and 48. 16.
cattle. Cp. Ps. 50. 10.
GOD. Heb. 'El. See Ap. 4. vowedst a vow. Fig. Polyptoton, Ap. 6 = madest a solemn vow.
Is there yet, &c.? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
Are we not, &c.? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
images. Heb. teraphim, a kind of household gods, showing that the idolatry of Babylonia still clung to Laban's family, in spite of his protestations in v. 29; 30. 27. Cp. v. 30; 35. 2.
unawares to Laban. Heb. stole the heart. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, heart being put for knowledge. Cp. v. 27. Rachel stole Laban's idols; and Jacob stole Laban's heart.
the river = the Euphrates. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Genus). Ap. 6. Gilead = perpetual fountain. Cp. Num. 32. 1, 39. Deut. 3. 12-16; 34. 1.
brethren. Fig. Synecdoche (of Species), Ap. 6, one relationship put for a general one.
good or bad. Heb. from good to bad.
What ... ? Figs. Erotesis and Aganactesis. Ap. 6.
Wherefore ... ? Fig. Erotesis (of Expostulation). Ap. 6. with mirth. Laban adds hypocrisy, covetousness, and avarice, to idolatry.
sons. Fig. Metonymy (of Species), Ap. 6, sons put for grandsons, &c. Cp. v. 55.

hand. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, hand put for the whole person, "in my power". you and your are plural. God of your father. In ch. 30. 27, 30, Laban had spoken of the LORD = Jehovah; now he has sunk so low as to say "your" God, and calls the teraphim "my gods".
sore longedst. Heb. with longing thou hast longed. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. my gods. Cp. on v. 29.
let him not live. This was in strict accordance with the Code of Khammurabi (§ 9), but in contrast with the Mosaic law. See Ap. 15.
33, 34 Rachel. Repeated by the Fig. Anadiplosis. Ap. 6. Heb. "tent of Rachel, and Rachel had taken."
furniture = saddle. searched = felt [with his hands].
my lord. Heb. the eyes of my lord. Fig. Prosopopoeia. Ap. 6. custom. Laban's deceit begets deceit.
twenty. The No. of disappointed expectancy. See Ap. 10.
my hand. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, hand put for "me". Cp. v. 29.

Thus I was. Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6) = "Thus (wherever) I was". drought = heat. Fig. Metonymy (of Effect), Ap. 6, effect put for the burning heat which caused it. Contrast with cold produced by the frost. my sleep. The Eastern shepherd often away from home for weeks at a time.
the fear. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6, fear put for the God Whom Jacob worshipped. with me = on my side. Ps. 118. 6, 7.
make. Heb. cut (Cp. 15. 10, 18) = solemnize.
pillar. Cp. 28. 18.
eat: i.e. of the covenant sacrifices. Cp. 26. 30. Ex. 24. 5, 11.
Jegar-sahadutha. Chaldaic = witness-heap. Galeed. Heb. same meaning.

Mizpah. Heb. watch-tower. he, i.e. Laban. So that he knew Heb. as well as Chaldee. the LORD. Laban also uses the name Jehovah. It is used by all the speakers in Gen. except the Nachash (ch. 3), Abimelech (when speaking to Abram, not to Isaac), the sons of Heth, Pharaoh, Joseph's brethren, and Joseph himself. absent. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct), Ap. 6 = Heb. hidden, put for absent.
man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. pillar. Distinct from the "heap". Cp. v. 45, 46.
offered sacrifice = killed beasts. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct). Ap. 6. Cp. Ap. 43. I. iv.
sons. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Part). Ap. 6. Put for grandsons as well. daughters. Also for granddaughters.

32. 1, 2. JACOB'S VISION AT MAHANAIM. The second vision, corresponding with that of Bethel: see 28. 10-22. See the structure on p. 32. went on his way. S. from Galeed and Mizpah. angels of God. Cp. Ps. 34. 7, to assure him of God's presence with him, and of His protection.
host = camp. Heb. mahaneh as in vv. 8, 21. Cp. Deut. 33. 2. Josh. 5. 14, 15. Ps. 27. 3; 78. 28; 106. 16. Mahanaim = two camps.

In n and n (vv. 7-32) note that Jacob alternately uses means as though there were no such thing as prayer; and then prays as though there were no such things as means. We may use means, but not trust in them. and. The Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6) shows the care with which he prepared. two bands = two camps. Same word (and perhaps idea) as in v. 2. See note.
Jacob's first prayer acknowledges both Elohim and Jehovah. saidst. Cp. v. 12 and 31. 13.

I am not worthy. Heb. I have proved unworthy. Fig. Heterosis (of Tense), Ap. 6. = I have been and am unworthy. mercies. Fig. Metonymy (of Cause). Ap. 6. First occ. of pl. my staff. Having nothing and deserving nothing but chastisement. Hence, the God who met him there (the God of Bethel) is "the God of Jacob", and is "the God of all grace" (1 Pet. 5. 10): cp. Ps. 146. 5.
with. Heb. upon. As though sons slain first and mothers falling on them.
saidst. Cp. v. 9 and 28. 13-15. as the sand. Fig. Paroemia. Ap. 6. See note on 13. 16.
present. See Ap. 43. II, iii.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
will appease him. Heb. "cover his face", i.e. hide my offence from him: "face" being put by Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, for himself. of me. Heb. my face. Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6.
Jabbok. Heb. pouring out, or emptying.
a Man. Heb. 'ish. Ap. 14. ii. Called "God" (vv. 28, 30), an "Angel", and Jehovah Elohim, Hos. 12. 4, 5. breaking. Heb. going up. Fig. Antimereia (of Verb Part. for noun). Ap. 6.
day breaketh. Heb. dawn hath ascended.
What is thy name? Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. For He knew his name.

Jacob = contender (25. 22). Used of the natural Jacob and his natural seed. Israel used for spiritual Jacob and his spiritual seed. Israel = "God commands, orders or rules". Man attempts it but always, in the end, fails. Out of some forty Hebrew names compounded with "El" or "Jah", God is always the doer of what the verb means (cp. Dani-el, God judges). prince = commander, orderer. Here used not to dignify but to reproach. Cp. Gen. 12. 15, princes (courtiers); 26. 26, chief of soldiers; 39. 1, officer; 40. 2, chief; 3, jailor; 47. 6, herdsmen; Ex. 1. 11, taskmasters, &c. hast thou power = hast thou contended. Jacob had contended with Esau in the womb, and thus got his name Jacob, which is referred to here in reproach, not in eulogy. men. Heb. pl. of 'ish, or 'enosh. Ap. 14. prevailed = succeeded. He had contended for the birthright and succeeded (25. 29-34). He had contended for the blessing and succeeded (27). He had contended with Laban and succeeded (31). He had contended with "men" and succeeded. Now he contends with God—and fails. Hence his name was changed to Isra-el, God commands, to teach him the greatly needed lesson of dependence upon God.
Peniel = Heb. God's face. seen. Cp. 16. 13. life = soul. Heb. nephesh. See Ap. 13.

he. Emph. to call attention to the fact that he was not only late, but limping. halted = limped. The sign that it is God who commands, and has real power to overcome. Typical of the national humiliation required before entering on the blessing.
sinew = the ligament of the hip joint.
men = Heb. sing. 'ish (Ap. 14), as we use the expression "400 foot". When pl., used only of angels.

and kissed him. This is one of the Heb. words with "extraordinary points", to show that the Massorites thought it should be omitted. See Ap. 31. It should read, "and fell on his neck and wept"; without kissing. This is the custom in Genesis. Cp. 45. 14; 46. 29.
enough = abundance, plenty.
Jacob said. Fig. Ellipsis (Ap. 6. ii b). Ellipsis should be supplied thus: "Jacob [refused, and] said.
men. Sam. and Sept. read "I".
What needeth it? Heb. What for? or Why so? Fig. Erotesis and Ellipsis (Ap. 6) = Why [have] anything?
house. The first we read of a house in connection with the Patriarchs. booths. Heb. succoth. Hence the name. First occ.
came to Shalem, a city of Shechem: read, came in peace to the city of Shechem; the Heb. Shalem means peace.
Hamor. Probably a title, like Abimelech and Pharaoh.
El-elohe-Israel—"GOD—the God-of-Israel", but not the place for this altar. Cp. 35. 1.

34. 1—37. 36. JACOB'S TROUBLE IN THE LAND. At Shechem, Dinah's disgrace, 34. Three burials: Deborah, 35. 8; Rachel (v. 20); and Isaac (35. 29). Joseph sold, 37. daughter of Leah. Cp. 30. 21, and own sister of Simeon and Levi, 29. 33, 34.
defiled. Heb. humbled.
his soul = himself. Fig. Synecdoche (of Part). Ap. 6. Heb. nephesh. kindly. Heb. on her heart (as though making an impression on it).
men. Heb. pl. of 'ish or 'enosh. See Ap. 14. iii. Israel. The first occ. in a collective sense.
soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. Fig. Synecdoche (of Part) and Pleonasm (Ap. 6), to emphasise the intensity of the longing.
gift. The noun put by Metonymy for the verb = ask me to give, &c. See Ap. 6.
deceitfully. Jacob's character his own scourge. The first and only occ. in Gen.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6.
Shall not, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.
edge. Heb. mouth. Fig. Pleonasm. Ap. 6. The acts of Jacob and his sons at Shechem may be contrasted with those of Abraham (12. 6), and of Joshua (Josh. 24. 1-27), and of Christ (John 4. 5).
The sons. Some MSS. read "And the sons".
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton, Ap. 6, to emphasise each item, in vv. 28, 29.
wealth. Heb. strength. Fig. Metonymy (of Adjunct). Ap. 6. Strength put for the wealth which it acquires.
Canaanites. Descendants of the Nephilim. See 12. 6 and Ap. 23 and 25. I ... I. Fig. Repetitio, Ap. 6, to emphasise Jacob's perturbation.
Should he ... ? Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4. Jacob. See notes on 32. 28; 43. 8; 45. 26, 28. Beth-el. House of GOD. Heb. El. Ap. 4 (28. 19). when. Cp. 27. 43.

Put away. Purification necessary in going up to Beth-el = the house of God. strange gods. Doubtless part of the spoils taken from the houses of the Shechemites. Cp. v. 4, and see 34. 28, 29. and. Fig. Polysyndeton. Ap. 6. be clean. First occ. Here and always used of ceremonial cleansing.
Jacob = Supplanter, or Contender. See on 32. 28; 43. 8; 45. 26, 28. earrings. Showing that the "strange gods" were part of the booty: probably of precious metals.
God. Heb. Elohim. Ap. 4.
El-Beth-el = GOD of the House of GOD. appeared: or revealed Himself. his brother. Some MSS., with Sam., Jon., Sept., Syr., read "Esau his brother".

Deborah Rebekah's nurse. We hear no more of Rebekah from the time Jacob left home (27. 45), not even of her death! Deborah may have come with a message, or she may, on Rebekah's death, have joined his household. Allon-bachuth. Heb. The oak of weeping.
Israel = GOD rules. See note on 32. 28.
GOD ALMIGHTY = Heb. El-Shaddai, GOD—the all-bountiful or all-sufficient. The title which best accords with the promise here given. Cp. 15. 1. kings. Fig. Metonymy (of Effect). Ap. 6.
I gave. Fig. Metonymy (of Subject). Ap. 6. = which I promised to give.
went up ... talked. Fig. Anthropopatheia. Ap. 6. He. i.e. God.

set up a pillar = Heb. pillared a pillar. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. poured a drink offering. See Ap. 15. First occurrence of "drink offering": afterward provided for in Lev. 23. 13, 18, 37, and in Num. 15. 5-10. Always "poured out," never drunk.
Ephrath. Heb. fertility.

her soul = her life. Heb. nephesh (Ap. 13), rendered "life" in 1. 20, 30; 9. 4, 5; 19. 17, 19; 32. 30; 44. 30. in departing = ebbing away, or failing (42. 28. Song 5. 6); or ending (Ex. 23. 16). In Ezek. 7. 10 rendered "gone forth"; Ex. 23. 26. In Ezek. 26. 18 rendered "departure". Ben-oni = Son of my sorrow. Benjamin = Son of my right hand. The word rendered "sorrow" ('avon) is a Homonym, the other meaning being "strength", and is so rendered in Gen. 49. 3. Deut. 21. 17. Job 18. 7, 12 &c. It is rendered "mourning" in Deut. 26. 14. Hos. 9. 4. This Homonym is the basis of Jacob's change of Benjamin's name. The A.V. and R.V. both recognize this Homonym.
Beth-lehem = House of bread.
grave. Heb. keber, first occ. 23. 4. = A sepulchre, from kabar to bury. Not sheol, which = THE grave. Cp. Ap. 35. unto this day. Well-known in the days of Samuel. See 1 Sam. 10. 2.
lay with. Cp. 49. 4. twelve. The number of governmental perfection. See Ap. 10. Fig. Synecdoche (of the Whole), Ap. 6. For the various orders of the twelve tribes, see Ap. 45.

27-29 (A, p. 36). The Death of Isaac. came. It does not follow that Jacob did not often see Isaac. As soon as Isaac was married, Abraham disappears from the history. It is the same with Isaac when Jacob married: and the same with Jacob when Joseph comes into prominence. They do not appear together in the history: but Abraham is described as "dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob" (Heb. 11. 9).
and died. Fig. Synonymia, Ap. 6, for great emphasis. They all mean the same thing, repeated in other words, to add solemnity to the event. was gathered. See note on 49. 33. 2 Sam. 12. 23.
generations. Given here, as no more is to be said about him.

Adah. Her second name was Bashemath, 26. 34. Aholibamah. Her second name was Judith, 26. 34; and her father, Anah, got a second name also from his discovery of the hot springs (see note on "mules", 36. 24). In 26. 34, called Hittite, because Hittite included Hivite. daughter. Sam., Sept., and Syr. read "son".
Bashemath also had a second name, Mahalath, 28. 9.

and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton, Ap. 6, pointing with emphasis to each item. persons = souls, Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13. Canaan. Esau's sons, born in the land went out of it. Jacob's sons, all born out of it and went into it. Jacob. "Unto Seir" should be added, according to Gb. Heb. Text.
Esau is Edom. Should be "Esau, he is Edom".
And these. See p. 45.
Teman. Whence came Eliphaz the Temanite. Job 2. 11; 15. 1.

Amalek. One of Israel's bitterest foes, with whom Jehovah has perpetual war, Ex. 17. 8, 14. Cp. Num. 24. 20. Deut. 25. 17-19. The land of A. so-called by Fig. Prolepsis (Ap. 6.), in Gen. 14. 7. sons. The "sons" of Adah are her son and grandsons.
dukes. Heb. chiefs, or, chieftains.
who inhabited, &c. The Horites were a branch of the Nephilim. See Ap. 23 and 25.
children = sons. Timna. Cp. v. 12.

both. Some codices, with Sam., Sept., and Syr., omit "both". found. Heb. matza, to happen on, discover (not invent); to find (not find out). mules. Heb. hayyemim, hot springs (with Vulg. and Syr.), hence Anah got the name of Beeri from Beer, a well, cp. 26. 34; and to distinguish him from the Anah of v. 20.
before there reigned. The ref. is to 17. 6 and 35. 11. Deut. 17. 14-20.
the river. i.e. the Euphrates.
The whole chapter, Fig. Hysterologia. Ap. 6. The last of the eleven Toledoth. Jacob. See notes on 32. 28; 43. 8; 45. 26, 28. wherein = of his father's sojournings.
Bilhah. i.e. Dan and Naphtali, 30. 6-8. Zilpah. i.e. Gad and Asher, 30. 10-13. his. Heb. their.

coat: with long sleeves, worn only by the chief and his heir. This the first cause of brothers' enmity. See note on 27. 15 and 25. 31. colours. Not "pieces". Marking it as priestly or royal. Ex. 28. 4, 39; 39. 1. 2 Sam. 13. 18, 19. Ps. 45. 14.
brethren. Heb. sons.
dreamed a dream. Fig. Polyptoton. Ap. 6. For emphasis = had a significant dream.
behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. in the field = in the midst of the field. stood upright. Heb. took its stand, or was set upright.
shalt thou, &c. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. Cp. the rejection of Moses, Ex. 2. 14; and of Christ, Luke 19. 14.
eleven stars = the eleven signs of the Zodiac, Joseph being the twelfth. See note on Num. 2. 2. made obeisance. Cp. 42. 6; 43. 26; 44. 14.
their father's flock. One of the fifteen expressions with the extraordinary points (see Ap. 31), indicating a doubtful reading, and suggesting that they had gone to feed themselves and make merry.
the flock. With the omission in v. 12 these words are unnecessary. Shechem. Was Jacob afraid after 34. 25-30?
man. Heb. 'ish. See Ap. 14. ii.
Dothan. On the high road to Egypt for caravans from the East.
conspired. Cp. Matt. 27. 1.
Behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. dreamer. Heb. master (or lord, Baal) of dreams.
and. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), emphasising the deliberateness of their actions.
him = his soul. Heb. nephesh. Ap. 13.
that he might rid him, &c. Fig. Parenthesis (Ap. 6), by way of explanation.
his coat. See on v. 3.

sat down. Showing their indifference. Cp. 42. 21 and Matt. 27. 36. behold. Fig. Asterismos. Ap. 6. company = caravan. There was a well-organized trade in sixteenth dynasty. Ishmeelites. So 39. 1. In vv. 28 and 36 called Midianites. Ishmael was the son of Abraham by Hagar (16. 11, 12); Midian the son of Abraham by Keturah (25. 2). See Judg. 8. 24, 25, where they were mixed together, and were distinguished only by their nose-rings. (Cp. 24. 47; 35. 4. Ex. 32. 2, &c.)
sell him. A Judas sold Joseph, and a Judas sold Christ. Slaves were in great demand in Egypt. were content = hearkened.
Midianites. See note on v. 25. they, i.e. Joseph's brethren. twenty. The number of disappointed expectancy. See Ap. 10.
whither. Fig. Erotesis. Ap. 6. go = go in, as though to hide himself.
killed. Heb. shahath. See Ap. 43. i, v.

And. Note the Fig. Polysyndeton (Ap. 6), in vv. 33, 34, to emphasise the successive steps in Jacob's grief. without doubt. Fig. Polyptoton (Ap. 6), "tearing he has been torn". Deceived by the blood of a kid, as he had deceived his father with the skin of a kid, 27. 16.
all his daughters. See on 30. 21, or it may be Synecdoche (of the Part), Ap. 6, put for all his female relatives and granddaughters. grave. Heb. Sheol, first occ. of word. See Ap. 35.
